# RPOW4 — Reusable Proofs of Work

> RPOW4 is a modern tribute to Hal Finney's 2004 Reusable Proofs of Work
> system. It's a browser-native, Bitcoin-style proof-of-work token network:
> sign up with an Ed25519 keypair, mine RPOW tokens by running SHA-256 in a
> Web Worker on your own CPU, send to other users, redeem bearer claim
> tokens, post to a public trollbox, and inspect a public ledger explorer.
> Live at https://rpow4.com. Source at https://github.com/cryptonaut420/rpow4.

RPOW4 is a centralized server-and-Postgres simulation, not a blockchain. It
keeps the spirit and tokenomics of Bitcoin (hard 21,000,000 RPOW supply cap,
50 RPOW initial block reward, halvings every 210,000 blocks, geometric sum
to exactly 21M) while replacing the IBM 4758 secure-coprocessor model of
Hal's original RPOW with modern wallet cryptography. Every state-changing
action is signed by the user's keypair; the server validates the signature
before applying the change. The server-signed token format keeps the
"reusable proof" abstraction Hal pioneered.

## What it is

- **Token network**: 21,000,000 RPOW hard cap. No premine, no founder
  allocation, no operator-held reserve. Every token in circulation was
  earned by an accepted proof of work.
- **Bitcoin-style schedule**: 50 RPOW per accepted PoW solution, halving
  every 210,000 blocks. Difficulty starts at 24 trailing-zero bits, steps
  up by +1 bit every ~164,000 blocks, capped at 50 bits so the chain stays
  mineable on commodity hardware long term.
- **Browser-native mining**: PoW runs in a Web Worker via `hash-wasm`
  SHA-256. The user mines in a tab; no installer, no external rig.
- **Ed25519 + BIP-39 / SLIP-0010 wallet**: keys live in the browser. The
  server only ever sees signatures and public keys.
- **Centralized ledger**: Postgres database operated by one person. If the
  server is breached, lost, or seized, balances may be lost with it. Treat
  it as a tribute / experiment, not a financial instrument.

## How to use it

1. **Create a wallet** at https://rpow4.com/#/login — pick "create new
   wallet", record the 12-word BIP-39 mnemonic offline, set a local
   password to encrypt it on this device, register a handle.
2. **Mine** — the sticky bottom bar contains the mining widget. Click
   `[ MINE ]`; the worker fetches a server-signed challenge with a random
   `nonce_prefix`, scans integer nonces, hashes
   `SHA-256(nonce_prefix || u64le(nonce))`, and submits when a hash has the
   required trailing-zero bits. The reward credits to your balance.
3. **Claim free tokens** at https://rpow4.com/#/faucet — once per cooldown
   window per (pubkey, IP). 5 RPOW per claim.
4. **Send** at https://rpow4.com/#/send — to a base58 pubkey or a registered
   handle. A small per-send fee (also halving-scheduled) is paid to the
   treasury.
5. **Create bearer claim tokens** at https://rpow4.com/#/claim — produces a
   signed link that anyone can redeem to receive the locked RPOW. Lets you
   gift tokens via URL.
6. **Browse the public ledger** at https://rpow4.com/#/explorer — every
   transaction, every account, full transaction history.
7. **Read the leaderboards** at https://rpow4.com/#/stats — top miners, top
   balances, network-wide aggregates.

## Pages on the site

- [Home / wallet](https://rpow4.com/): your wallet — balance, history, send/receive shortcuts.
- [Send](https://rpow4.com/#/send): transfer RPOW to another pubkey or handle.
- [Claim](https://rpow4.com/#/claim): create a bearer-token claim URL anyone can redeem.
- [Activity](https://rpow4.com/#/activity): your personal transaction feed.
- [Stats](https://rpow4.com/#/stats): network stats, leaderboards (top miners and richest accounts), share-of-supply per account.
- [Explorer](https://rpow4.com/#/explorer): public ledger feed, search by tx id / pubkey / handle, account detail pages.
- [Faucet](https://rpow4.com/#/faucet): claim free tokens once per cooldown window.
- [Trollbox](https://rpow4.com/#/trollbox): a fee-paying public chat — each post burns a small RPOW fee to the treasury.
- [About](https://rpow4.com/#/ledger): live ledger snapshot + project description and lineage.
- [History](https://rpow4.com/#/history): the historical record behind RPOW — Hal Finney's 2004 announcement, cypherpunk manifestos, Satoshi's whitepaper, and related primary sources.
- [Docs](https://rpow4.com/#/docs): full API reference, hand-verified against the route source.
- [Ecosystem](https://rpow4.com/#/ecosystem): directory of related RPOW projects (RPOW2, RPOW3, rpowmarket, swap, CLI tooling).

## API (public, JSON)

Base URL: `https://rpow4.com` (the same origin serves both the web app and
the API; the SPA proxies everything under `/auth`, `/challenge`, `/mint`,
`/send`, `/me`, `/activity`, `/ledger`, `/stats`, `/explorer`, `/lookup`,
`/signup`, `/claim`, `/faucet`, `/trollbox` to the Fastify server). Full
reference with examples is at https://rpow4.com/#/docs.

### Read endpoints (public, no auth)

- `GET /health` — liveness probe.
- `GET /ledger` — current network state: total minted, circulating supply,
  block height, current reward, current difficulty, current send and
  trollbox fees (both halving-scheduled), treasury balance, total fees,
  user count, faucet claim count, total faucet dripped.
- `GET /ledger/events` — paginated newest-first global event stream.
- `GET /explorer/feed` — recent transactions; filter `?type=mint|transfer`.
- `GET /explorer/tx/:id` — transaction detail by UUID.
- `GET /explorer/account/:pubkey` — account summary + paginated history.
- `GET /lookup/:name` — resolve a handle to a pubkey.
- `GET /stats/leaderboard?sort=balance|minted` — top 100 accounts.
- `GET /faucet` — current faucet eligibility / cooldown / treasury.
- `GET /trollbox` — paginated newest-first message feed + current post fee.
- `GET /.well-known/rpow-pubkey.pem` — the server's Ed25519 signing pubkey
  (used to verify server-signed token payloads).

### Write endpoints (require an Ed25519 signature over a canonical body)

- `POST /signup/challenge` + `POST /signup` — register a pubkey + handle,
  gated by a small client-side proof-of-work to slow handle squatters.
- `POST /auth/challenge` + `POST /auth/session` — pubkey-based login. The
  server hands the client a short-lived envelope; the client signs it; the
  server returns a session cookie.
- `POST /auth/logout` — destroy the session.
- `POST /me/display_name` — set or clear your handle.
- `POST /challenge` + `POST /mint` — request a mining challenge, then submit
  a solution. Mint requires a session AND a wallet signature over
  `('mint', { challenge_id, solution_nonce })`.
- `POST /send` — transfer RPOW to a recipient. Requires a wallet signature
  and an idempotency key.
- `POST /claim` + `POST /claim/:id/redeem` + `POST /claim/:id/cancel` —
  bearer claim-token lifecycle.
- `POST /faucet/claim` — credit your account from the treasury, subject to
  per-pubkey + per-IP cooldown.
- `POST /trollbox` — post a message; burns the current trollbox fee to the
  treasury (the fee halves alongside the block reward).

All canonical signing payloads are documented in
`packages/shared/src/canonical.ts` in the source repo.

## Tokenomics one-liner

50 RPOW × 210,000 blocks × Σ (1/2)ⁿ = exactly 21,000,000 RPOW. Same
geometric series as Bitcoin. Both the per-send fee and the trollbox post
fee bit-shift right by the current halving index, so user-paid network
costs decay at the same cadence as the block reward.

## Lineage

RPOW4 builds on community RPOW ports that came before it:

- [RPOW2](https://github.com/frkrueger/rpow) — the first modern web-app
  revival of Hal's idea. Direct ancestor of this project.
- [RPOW3](https://github.com/arben777/rpow3) — continued the lineage with
  hashcash mining and Ed25519-signed tokens.
- [RPOW4](https://github.com/cryptonaut420/rpow4) — this site.

The chain traces back to Hal Finney's
[original 2004 announcement](https://nakamotoinstitute.org/finney/rpow/).
The full ecosystem (live sites, swaps, prediction markets, CLI tooling) is
listed at https://rpow4.com/#/ecosystem.

## Caveats

- **Centralized**: ledger lives in one Postgres database. No 51%-attack
  story, no decentralized recovery — operator can take the server offline,
  data could be lost. Use it accordingly.
- **No warranty**: the project is a tribute / educational experiment. No
  responsibility taken for breaches, downtime, lost balances.
- **Wallet keys live in your browser**: lose the mnemonic, lose the
  account. There is no server-side recovery.
